Highlights: Q2 (July-September), FY 2026-27 The Company achieved its highest-ever quarterly total sales volume of 696,654 units, registering a growth of 26.5% over the same period previous year. The Company’s growth in the domestic passenger vehicle market was broad-based, with small car sales increasing by 35.9% and SUV sales by 68.2%. The Company’s recently introduced SUVs received a strong market response and contributed to this robust growth. The Company’s domestic market share increased by 2.2 percentage points to 40.8%. Recent capacity additions have enabled the Company to serve the strong demand. Even with enhanced production capacity, demand continued to outpace supply resulting in a low network inventory of about 17 days and pending bookings of about 200,000 units at the end of the quarter. In export markets, despite the challenging geopolitical situation, the Company could achieve sales of 108,119 units in Q2 FY 2026-27, as compared to 110,487 units in Q2 FY25-26. During the quarter, the Company registered its highest-ever Net Sales of INR 506,155 million against INR 401,358 million in the same period of the previous year. The Operating Profit (EBIT) in the quarter stood at INR 28,037 million as compared to INR 33,820 million in Q2 FY25-26 owing to West-Asia conflict linked commodity increases. Sequentially this translated to a growth of 10.8% from Q1 FY26-27 to Q2 FY26-27. However, non-operating income declined sharply in Q2 owing to mark-to-market losses on invested surplus. With this, the Net Profit for the quarter stood at INR 24,149 million compared to INR 33,028 million the same period previous year. The Company posted its highest-ever half-yearly Net Sales of INR 1,005,746 million in H1 FY 2026-27 as compared to INR 767,564 million in H1 FY 2025-26. Yours faithfully, For DCM Shriram Limited (Deepak Gupta) Company Secretary & Compliance Officer Encl: As above PRESS RELEASE DCM Shriram Reports 22% Revenue Growth in Q2 FY27 at ₹3,977 Crore • H1 FY27 revenue grows 15% to ₹7,541 crore; strategic investments in downstream integration, cost management and operational reliability and efficiency gather momentum • Board announced an interim dividend of 200% amounting to Rs. 62.38 crores. New Delhi, October 26, 2026: DCM Shriram Ltd, a diversified and integrated conglomerate, announced its consolidated financial results for the second quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026. The Company reported consolidated net revenue, net of excise duty, of ₹3,977 crore in Q2 FY27, registering a growth of 22% over ₹3,272 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue growth was driven by Chemicals & Vinyl, Sugar & Ethanol, Fenesta Building Systems and Fertilizer businesses. PBDIT for the quarter stood at ₹319 crore, compared with ₹408 crore in Q2 FY26, a decline of 22%, primarily reflecting higher input costs in Chemicals and lower earnings in the Agri input businesses. The previous year's quarter also included a one-time positive impact of Rs 76 crore towards incentive from the Government of Gujarat in the chemicals business and Rs 15.5 crores in Sugar business on account of upward revision in power rates. Profit After Tax (PAT) stood at ₹106 crore against ₹159 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. For H1 FY27, consolidated net revenue, net of excise duty, increased 15% to ₹7,541 crore from ₹6,534 crore in H1 FY26. PBDIT stood at ₹683 crore compared with ₹734 crore last year. Reported PAT increased to ₹799 crore from ₹273 crore, including a favourable tax adjustment of ₹474.3 crore and exceptional gains of ₹79.4 crore. Effective normal PAT was ₹253 crore. Business Performance Highlights Chemicals: The business revenue grew 47% to ₹1,343 crore, supported by improved ECU realisations, and contributions from advanced materials value chain. The commissioning of the Aluminium Chloride plant and partial commissioning of the Calcium Chloride plant at Bharuch further strengthened downstream integration. Vinyl: Vinyl revenue increased 20% to ₹234 crore, with improved volumes and realisations supporting profitability. Sugar & Ethanol: Revenue increased 10% to ₹1,023 crore, while PBDIT grew 85% to ₹62 crore. Higher domestic sugar prices and improved ethanol margins supported performance, despite lower sugar sales volumes. Ethanol sales volumes increased 24% during the quarter, a timing difference.
